sentences.text:
Hereinafter, the parties are being referred to by their original status in the Application i.e.,
Appellants as 'Complainants' and Respondent Nos.2 to 4 as 'Accused'.
2) Heard Mr.Nashikkar, learned Advocate for the Appellants, Mr.Gavand, learned A.P.P. for Respondent No.1-State, Mr.Upadhyay, learned Advocate for Respondent Nos.2 and 3 and Ms.Khurana, learned Advocate for Respondent No.4.
Perused the record.
3) The Complainants had filed the said Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.293 of 2022 wherein it was narrated that, accused No.1 is a registered limited company.
It is engaged in the business of development of real estate, construction and other allied activities.
Accused Nos.2 and 3 are Directors of accused No.1.
In November 2014, the accused persons informed the Complainants that,

accused No.1 has acquired rights in respect of total 43 ares of land in Survey No.63, Hissa Nos.2 and 3, at Village Kharadi, District Pune for development and construction of buildings, comprising of flats and tenements.
Said land was owned by M/s. Bhujbal Brothers.

That, the accused persons floated an investment scheme in the nature of 'Buy Back Scheme' wherein accused persons would accept investments from the Complainants for a period of 12 months and against which they would give lucrative returns and also informed that, certain H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.doc built up/investment area will be allotted as and by way of security to the Complainants.

It was also informed that, on expiry of the said 12 months period, the Complainants will have to sell back the built up/investment area, however, they will be entitled to the return of the invested amount along with the returns promised.
3.1) That, relying upon the said representations and assurances by the accused, which evidently were malicious, the Complainants agreed to invest US$ 80000 in the aforesaid scheme against which an investment area/built-up area of 1261 sq. ft. was offered to Complainant No.2 and the Complainants were promised the return of US$ 111000 upon expiry of 12 months period therefrom.

It is alleged that, in view of aforesaid understanding the Complainant No.2 and the accused persons entered into the 'Articles of Agreement' dated 14th November, 2014 incorporating the terms of the investment and other relevant details.

3.2) It is alleged that, pursuant to the request of accused No.3 via e-mail dated 14th November, 2014 the Complainant No.2 transferred US$ 5,000 between 7th November and 26th November 2014 as investment, in the bank account of Accused No.4, who is son of Accused No.3.
Said e-mail was also marked to Complainant No.1.
Pursuant another request of accused No.3 via e-mail dated 17th November, 2014 the Complainant No.2 transferred US$ 75,000 as investment in the bank account of M/s.
Cathay
H. C. Shiv

Cotton (Hk) Ltd.

3.3) It is alleged that, around December 2015, upon expiry of the 12 months investment period,
when Complainant No.1 requested the accused to pay the promised returns of US$ 1,11,000, the accused persons did not pay the said amount on a pretext of financial crisis.
Therefore, the parties renewed the 'Articles of Agreement' on 7 th January, 2016 whereby the investment period was extended till next 12 months and the accused persons promised to pay US$ 1,46,520.
It is alleged that, on expiration of the 12 months extended period in January 2017, the Complainant No.1 again requested the accused to pay US$ 1,46,520 as promised earlier.

However, giving the same reason of Amit Ghoshal S/O Mr. Tapan Ghoshal And ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116589929/
3 financial crisis again, the accused persons requested to renew the investment for further six months giving assurance to pay total US$ 1,58,241 including further returns.

Thereafter in June 2017, when Complainant No.1 on behalf of Complainant No.2 requested the accused persons to pay US$
1,58,241, the accused persons requested for more time and assured to pay the said amount by February/April 2018.
Thereafter, the Complainants followed up with the accused but it vain.

Thus,
the accused persons deceived the Complainants dishonestly and induced them to invest US$ 80,000 in their fraudulent scheme by giving allurement of good returns and misappropriated said amount for their own benefit.

Therefore, the Complainants sent a written H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.doc complaint of the offence by RPAD to Chandan Nagar Police Station, Pune and the Commissioner of Police, Pune on 5th February, 2022.
Thereafter, statement of Complainant No.1 was recorded on 1 st March, 2022.
However, the concerned Police Station did not take cognizance of the written complaint by registering the F.I.R. against accused persons.
This led to filing of said Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.293 of 2022.

4) After considering the Application, the documents enclosed and the submissions made by Advocate for Complainants, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune in its impugned order noted that, in the month of December 2015, the Complainants were aware that the accused were not in a position to repay the invested amount.
The Complainants, however, renewed the investment.
Thereafter, the accused persons did not pay the money claimed.
Hence, the Complainants sent a legal notice to accused on 19th January, 2022 but it was of no use.
Hence, ultimately, the Complainants sent their written complaint to police by RPAD on 5 th February, 2022.
The transaction between Complainants and accused persons was based on 'Article of Agreement'.
However, for 7 years, the Complainants have not taken any step against the accused.
This all indicate that, the Complainants knew that, the transaction in question was of civil nature, therefore till 5th February, 2022 they did not approach to police nor the concerned Court.
In the 'Articles of Agreement' dated 14 th November H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.doc 2014, at para no.8, it was mentioned that, all disputes shall be referred to the Arbitrator.
It is evident from the said fact that, the transaction between Complainants and accused persons is of civil nature.

As such, the Complainants failed to make out a satisfactory ground to hold that, since beginning accused persons had intention to cheat the Complainants, which warrants a direction to register the F.I.R. and investigation against the accused.
In this background, the learned Judge dismissed the Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.293 of 2022.
Hence, Appeal.
5) Mr.Nashikkar, learned Advocate for the Appellants submitted that, the accused persons floated a wholly nonviable scheme of investment and returns.
This conduct manifests that, since inception there was intention on the part of the accused to cheat the Complainant.
Therefore, the accused persons invited the investment and later on siphoned that money to shell entities/sister companies.
Thus, this is a clear case of cheating and misappropriation.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, it is evident that, the amount invested in the scheme was a 'Deposit' and the accused were falling in the expression 'Financial Establishments', as defined in Section 2(c) and 2(d) of the M.P.I.D. Act, respectively.
However, the learned Judge completely ignored the above and erroneously held that, the transaction in question was of civil nature.
Therefore, the impugned Order is not sustainable in law and liable H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.doc to be quashed.
To buttress his submissions, the learned Advocate placed his reliance on following decisions.

8) The entire claim of Complainant No.2 in the Application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. was based on two 'Articles of Agreements'.
H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.doc
However, the signature of the Complainant No.2 on the 1 st Agreement is forged.
We have compared it personally in Court with the assistance of learned Advocate for the Appellants and found that it is forged i.e., somebody else has signed it.
The complaint sent to the police on 5 th February, 2022 also carrying a forged signature of the Complainant No.2, who is the actual victim of the crime.

On comparison of the said forged signatures of Complainant No.2 with the signatures of Complainant No.1 and the patterns of said signatures, it is apparent that, the Complainant No.1 himself forged the said signatures of Complainant No.2.
These circumstances indicate that, the said complaint was sent by Complainant No.1, not by Complainant No.2.
The POA was not in existence on the said date and only general stamp was added to that subsequently.

As such, there was no lawful compliance of Section 154(1)
and (3) of Cr.P.C. before filing of the Application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.

Such compliance is mandatory in view of the decisions in the case of Priyanka Srivastava and Anr. vs. State of U.P. and Ors., (2015) 6 SCC 287 and Sayed Anwar Ahmed and Anr. vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr., 2017 SCC OnLine Bom 3972.
9) Even though in the Application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. it was claimed that, the accused persons had floated an investment in the nature of 'Buy Back Scheme', in the 'Articles of Amit Ghoshal S/O Mr. Tapan Ghoshal And ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116589929/

sentences.text: This circumstance clearly indicate that, the Complainant No.2 entered into this transaction on his own, after understanding the entire background of the scheme and consequences thereof.

Similarly,
from the subsequent 'Articles of Agreement' it can be seen that, on maturity of the initial investment period, Complainant No.2 himself agreed to re-invest the said investment for further period.
This subsequent Agreement does not mention that, the re-investment was on account of the request of the accused persons as they were facing financial crisis.
This Agreement does not bear signature of Complainant No.2.
10) According to the Complainants, the entire US$ 80,000 were paid to the accused persons as investment.
However, the Complainants have not explained as to why US$ 75,000 were deposited in the bank account of M/s.Cathay Cotton (Hk) Ltd.
On query by this Court, the Advocate for the Appellants stated that, said amount of US$ 80,000 was shown as loan in the Income Tax returns of Complainant No.2.
In the backdrop, the learned Advocate for the Appellants stated that, there is no material to attract the offence of Section 409 of the I.P.C. and the offences under the M.P.I.D. Act.

The Complainant No.1 is not victim of the alleged offence.
11) Admittedly, the accused persons had assured to repay the  H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.do invested amount alongwith the assured return in February/April 2018.
However, till issuing the demand notice dated 19 th January, 2022 no steps were taken by the Complainants to recover the invested amount.

12) In view of the above discussion, we are of the opinion that, the subject monetary transaction between the Complainant No.2 and the accused party was purely an unauthorised money lending transaction.
As such, undoubtedly, the dispute between them was of civil in nature.
The Complainant No.1 is not victim of the alleged offence.

However, it seems that, the Complainant No.2 was trying to recover his time barred debt with the help of Complainant No.1, by filing the said Application for setting the criminal law in motion.
13) Be that as it may.
Bare reading of the 'Articles of Agreements' clearly denotes that, on his own the Complainant No.2 invested his money willingly in the 'Buy Back Scheme'' floated by the accused.
Amit Ghoshal S/O Mr. Tapan Ghoshal And ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116589929/
6 Therefore, it cannot be said that, the accused persons deceived the Complainant No.2 and dishonestly induced him to enter into the said investment scheme and the Agreements.
From the careful reading of the Agreements it seems that, the Complainant No.2 entered into the said transaction only to earn an exorbitant interest but knowingly taking risk of his money.

That apart,
huge money was deposited with M/s.Cathay Cotton (Hk) Ltd. and not in India.

This indicate that,
the Appellants are trying to suppress something material H. C. Shiv 1 APEAL614.2023 FINAL.doc from this Court and have not approached the Court with clean hands.
Therefore, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune has rightly held that, this is a civil dispute.

14) In so far as the reported cases cited by the learned Advocate for the Complainants are concerned,
the facts of the said cases and the case in hand are distinct.
15) In view thereof, we find no illegality in the impugned Order.
As a result, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
